title: Update an approved enabler with a prompt
prompt:
# Story 7: Update an approved enabler with a prompt

- **Story**: XXX-update-enabler
- **Created**: 2026-11-09
- **Status**: Draft
- **Demo**: open `0003-set-up-postgresql-and-flyway.md`, see the prompt turn into "Editing ...", write "Add a task to verify the migration
  on an empty database", read the draft that starts from the enabler's own text, press "Apply changes", and see the open file change.

## Story

As a team member, I want to open an architectural enabler and describe a change in the prompt, so that the AI updates **that** enabler from
its current text, its ADRs and its links, and I do not end up with a second enabler for what is the same work.

## Creating and updating are different

| | Creating (stories 1 to 4) | Updating (this story) |
|---|---|---|
| When | no file is open, or a driver or an ADR is open | an **enabler** is open (and no draft is on screen) |
| The prompt says | "Describe the architectural enabler..." | "Describe the change to make to this enabler..." |
| The user chooses | the ADRs (required) and the links | nothing: the enabler's own ADRs and links are used |
| Number and path | a new number and slug | the enabler's own, which never change |
| The model gets | the description of new work | **the enabler's current text**, with a requested change |
| Approving | "Approve and create enabler": a new enabler | "Apply changes": the text of the enabler is replaced |
| Stored | a new enabler, its first prompt | only the text (and the title read from it) |

## Acceptance tests

The prompt follows the opened file

- [ ] **Given** an approved enabler, **When** the user opens it (from the tree, from the card of a message, or from a chip of "Derives from"
  or "Linked to"), **Then** the prompt column changes: a chip with a pencil and the text "Editing
  architectural-enablers/0003-<slug>.md" (in the colour of enablers) takes the place of the Link button, the ADR panel is not shown, the
  box says "Describe the change to make to this enabler...", and the send button is named "Draft changes to this enabler".
- [ ] **Given** the enabler is open and there is no conversation yet, **Then** the column shows "What should change?" and "Describe the
  change. Claude drafts the updated file, and it replaces the current text once you approve it.", and no examples.
- [ ] **Given** the box has text, **Then** the send button is enabled. No ADR is needed, since the enabler has its own.
- [ ] **Given** the user closes the file, or opens a driver or an ADR (which are immutable), **Then** the prompt is for a new enabler again
  (story 1): the ADR panel and the Link button are back and the chip is gone.
- [ ] **Given** the user had typed text before opening the enabler, **Then** the text stays in the box when the prompt changes.
- [ ] **Given** a draft is on screen (a new enabler or an update), **When** the user opens another file, **Then** the prompt keeps revising
  that draft (story 4). A new target is taken only when no draft is on screen.
- [ ] **Given** the file panel of the enabler, **Then** its lock says "Read-only here. Describe the change in the prompt to update this
  enabler." in place of the note of story 3. It still has no Save, Delete, Sync, "Add link" or "Cross enabler" control, and no text box.

Sending the change

- [ ] **Given** a change, **When** the user presses Enter (or the button), **Then** the box is cleared, the text shows as a message on the
  right, and a draft card appears with the enabler's **own** path `architectural-enablers/0003-<slug>.md` and the chip "Writing...". No new
  number is taken. The card shows no chips of ADRs or links.
- [ ] **Given** the request, **Then** the model gets the **project context** of story 5, unchanged, so it comes from the prompt cache as it
  does for a new enabler (the opened enabler's scope is in it, as for every enabler).
- [ ] **Given** the request, **Then** it says "Document type: architectural enabler", "Task: edit an existing document", "File:
  architectural-enablers/0003-<slug>.md" and today's date. It has **no** "Assigned identifier".
- [ ] **Given** the request, **Then** it has "## Derives from (ADRs)" with the ADRs **of the opened enabler**, and "## Linked documents (full
  text)" with those ADRs and the documents it links to, in full (the rules of story 6), and, through its linked enablers, the documents one
  step further, **without the opened enabler itself** even if one of them links back to it.
- [ ] **Given** the request, **Then** it has "## Existing architectural enablers" (all of them, the opened one too) and "## Existing
  stories", as in story 5.
- [ ] **Given** the request, **Then** it has "## Current document" with the stored text of the enabler (trimmed) and "## Requested change"
  with the user's text, in that order, at the end.
- [ ] **Given** the enabler was updated before, **Then** the next request's "Current document" is the updated text.
- [ ] **Given** the system prompt, **Then** it tells the model that when the task is to edit an existing document, the current document is
  given and it returns the **complete** document with only the requested change applied, keeping the identifier, the creation date and
  everything the change does not touch.

Following, revising and discarding the draft

- [ ] **Given** the update draft, **Then** everything of story 2 holds for it (the chip, Stop, Retry, the incomplete note, the error, the token
  chips), and a Ready draft can be revised as in story 4: the box says "Ask for changes to the draft...", and the turns sent are the first
  request, the draft, and the change.
- [ ] **Given** a Ready draft of an update, **Then** the approve button reads "Apply changes" (not "Approve and create enabler"), and is
  enabled only when the draft is Ready.
- [ ] **Given** the user presses Discard, **Then** the draft disappears and the enabler is exactly as it was.

Applying

- [ ] **Given** the user presses "Apply changes", **Then** the stored text of **that** enabler is replaced by the draft (trimmed, with one final
  newline). The id, the number, the slug, the first prompt, the date of creation, the ADRs it derives from and its links are **not**
  changed. No enabler is added, so the folder's count stays.
- [ ] **Given** the enabler is open, **Then** the file panel shows the new text at once, in the rendered view and in the Markdown view,
  without being opened again.
- [ ] **Given** applying, **Then** two messages are added: the user's text, and "Applied. I updated architectural-enablers/0003-<slug>.md.",
  with the card that opens the file.
- [ ] **Given** applying, **Then** the draft is gone, the box is empty, and the prompt is still about the same enabler.
- [ ] **Given** the new text has a first `# ` line, **Then** the title of the enabler is read from it again, and the tree tooltip and the
  labels (`AE-0003. <title>`) follow. **Given** it has none, **Then** the old title stays.
- [ ] **Given** the page is reloaded, **Then** the updated text is still there. **Given** two projects, **Then** each keeps its own.
- [ ] **Given** an update draft is on screen and the user opens another file, **Then** the card still names the enabler it will update, and
  "Apply changes" updates **that** one, not the file that is open.

What the updated enabler is like (checked by reading drafts from a real model; they are not automated)

- [ ] **Given** a change, **Then** the draft changes only what was asked, keeps the title line `# AE-0003. ...`, the Created date and the
  "Implements ADR(s)" line, and is still in the template of story 5.
- [ ] **Given** a change that conflicts with an Accepted ADR, **Then** the draft leaves that part out and names it under Out of scope.
- [ ] **Given** a change that another enabler already covers, **Then** the draft does not take it over.
- [ ] **Given** a change that only adds one task, **Then** the other tasks and the Definition of done are as they were.

## Business rules and constraints

- **The opened enabler is the context of the prompt.** Which enabler the prompt is about is decided by the file that is open, and by nothing
  else. Only an enabler can be the target here: a driver and an ADR are immutable (`story-builder-folders.md`).
- **Updating never creates.** It takes no number, makes no slug and stores no new prompt, date, link or ADR. The ADRs and the links chosen
  when the enabler was created cannot be changed by this prompt.
- **The text of the enabler is the only thing that changes**, and its title is read from the new text.
- The AI only drafts. The user decides, with "Apply changes", and a Discard leaves everything as it was.
- A draft is one thing at a time: while one is on screen (new or update), the prompt works on it, whatever file is open.
- Everything else about drafts is as in stories 2, 4 and 5: the states, the revision, the 40 turns, the context and the cache.

## Out of scope

- Editing the text by hand (a text box with Save and Ctrl+S). In the spike this locks the prompt while there are unsaved changes ("Save or
  discard your manual changes, then describe the change."). It comes with manual editing.
- Changing the ADRs or the links of an enabler (from the file or by prompt), the *Cross enabler* flag, deleting, marking it Done, and
  synchronising it with the repository.
- Undoing an update, a history of versions, and comparing the old and new text.
- Updating a story, a driver or an ADR (stories have their own stories; the others are immutable here).
- A warning when an enabler that stories already build on is changed.

## Tasks

- [ ] Split the single `editable` flag of an entry into "the prompt can change it" and "the file panel can edit it by hand", and give an
  enabler the first only.
- [ ] Choose the target of the prompt from the open file: an enabler is the target when no draft is on screen; anything else is not.
- [ ] Change the composer for a target: the "Editing ..." chip, no ADR panel and no Link button, the placeholder, the button name, the
  heading "What should change?" and no examples, and the send rule without the ADR.
- [ ] Build the request for a change: document type, "Task: edit an existing document", the file, the date, the enabler's ADRs and links in
  full, one step through its linked enablers without itself, the lists, "Current document" and "Requested change".
- [ ] Start the draft in edit mode with the enabler's own path and no number, and keep the target in the draft.
- [ ] Change the approve button to "Apply changes" for an update.
- [ ] Add `applyEdit` for an enabler to the store: replace the text, read the title again, and add the two messages, in one save.
- [ ] Make the open file panel show the new text at once, and change its note.
- [ ] Test: the target rules (enabler, driver, ADR, none, with a draft), the request for a change (the exact text for a small project, without
  the identifier, without the enabler itself in the links), apply, discard, the title, reload, and a draft that outlives the open file.

tasks.text: Split the single `editable` flag on a builder entry into two flags: one for prompt-driven editing and one for hand-editing in the file panel; mark approved enablers as prompt-editable only (ADR-0007)

Implement target selection: when no draft is on screen and the open file is an approved enabler, set that enabler as the prompt target; clear the target when the file is closed or a non-enabler file is opened

Update the composer component to render editing mode: the "Editing …" chip, hidden ADR panel and Link button, updated placeholder, updated send-button label, "What should change?" heading, and no examples; restore new-enabler mode when the target is cleared (ADR-0007, ADR-0016)

Build the request payload for an edit: document type, task, file path, date, no identifier, the enabler's own ADRs and linked documents in full (one step through linked enablers, excluding the enabler itself), the full project context lists, "## Current document", and "## Requested change" (ADR-0017)
Add the edit instruction to the system prompt so the model returns the complete document with only the requested change applied (ADR-0007)
Start the draft in edit mode: record the target enabler's path and id in the draft, assign no new number, and show no ADR or link chips on the draft card
Change the approve button label to "Apply changes" for an edit draft and gate it on the Ready state
Implement `applyEdit` in the store: replace the enabler's stored text, re-read the title from the first `# ` line, append the two confirmation messages, and persist in a single save (ADR-0017)
Update the file panel to re-render immediately on apply without requiring the file to be reopened, and update the read-only note to the editing-mode wording

Write unit tests: target selection rules (enabler, driver, ADR, no file, with a draft in progress), request payload shape (no identifier, no self-reference in linked documents), apply (text replaced, title updated, messages added), discard (text unchanged), title fallback, persistence across reload, and a draft that outlives the open file (ADR-0005, ADR-0016)
Make an approved enabler the target of the prompt without making it editable by hand: the open file carries the identity of the enabler, and the panel stays read-only (ADR-0007)

Build the request for an edit in the backend, from the identity of the enabler and the change: document type, task, file path, date, no identifier, the ADRs of the enabler by label, its linked documents in full (one step through linked enablers, excluding the enabler itself), the existing enablers and stories, "## Current document", and "## Requested change", after the project context of story 028; refuse an unknown enabler before the model is called (ADR-0017)

Implement the update in the backend (command and handler, `update` on the repository and its JPA adapter, `PUT` on the enabler with OpenAPI): replace the enabler's stored text, re-read the title from the first `# ` line, append the two confirmation messages, in one transaction (ADR-0017, ADR-0011, ADR-0014)

Write Jest unit and acceptance tests: target selection rules (enabler, driver, ADR, no file, with a draft in progress), the request carrying the identity of the enabler, apply (text replaced, title updated, messages added, panel and tree refreshed), refusal and failure with the button pressable again, discard (text unchanged), title fallback, persistence with the browser's storage cleared, and a draft that outlives the open file (ADR-0005, ADR-0016)

Write JUnit tests for the domain and the application (revise, title, messages, unknown enabler, the exact edit request, no Accepted check, the cap of 40 turns), a Testcontainers test for the update and its persistence, REST controller tests (200, 400, 404 and the draft field), and an ArchUnit rule that the new command and adapters stay in their hexagonal layers (ADR-0005, ADR-0009, ADR-0012, ADR-0014)
